workingStandard: The author considers the initial supported holdout errors (about 0.23 m ground and 0.25 m streets) close to the required accuracy. Use this as a first-pass baseline; prioritise sparse coverage, large discrepancies and consequential bank/structure/flow-path joins over marginal residual improvements.
streetInterpretation: Street dots constrain the developed surface. Lanes through marsh can approximate neighbouring ground where better evidence is absent. The author expects lanes often to be only slightly raised and ordinary historical street fill generally limited; test local exceptions without imposing a fixed fill correction.
scope: These are review decisions for an interpolation experiment. No new 3D terrain or flood-solver levels have been applied.

targetedChecks.finding: Full mosaic and 8x crop inspected. The 3.4 figure and separate dot above it lie within the lane, beside the L of LANE. No bank hatching surrounds this dot. Nearby lane readings are also low, while some streets to the north are higher.
targetedChecks.decision: Retain the existing 3.4 ft road observation. Its approximately +2.15 m holdout prediction error is a warning about smoothing over local relief, not a reason to raise or reject the observed lane. No adjoining marsh height or fill thickness is established by this dot.

targetedChecks.surface: Campbell Road beside the railway cutting, south of the bridge
targetedChecks.finding: Full mosaic, 8x dot crop and 3x context inspected. 44.9 is clear and its dot lies in Campbell Road beside the railway cutting, south of the bridge. Nearby bridge-area readings reach 45.0 ft; adjoining roads are lower. This is a real recorded local high point, not a digit error. The map does not by itself quantify natural relief versus made ground.
targetedChecks.decision: Retain 44.9 ft as a road-surface constraint. Its roughly -2.19 m held-out prediction discrepancy flags the need to preserve local street profiles and railway-cutting geometry. Do not lower it to neighbouring street averages or extend the road level onto the railway floor.

floodInterpretation: The author accepts about 30 cm as a useful working terrain accuracy target because historical high-water levels and other flood inputs are imprecise. The reported 23–25 cm holdout errors are averages on supported predictions, not a universal 30 cm error bound. Evaluate plausible water-level ranges against broad historical flood extent and flow routes; prioritise consequential barriers and connections rather than an exact inundation outline. Regional hydraulic calibration remains unfinished.
